```python
import socket

import pytest

from recordings import alerts
from recordings.alerts import AlertConfig, ping_deadman, send
from recordings.config import ConfigError, load_config


def test_an_alert_posts_to_the_topic_with_title_priority_and_tags(ntfy):
    ac = AlertConfig(ntfy_server=ntfy.url, topic="topic-do-not-print_1", deadman_url=None)
    assert send(ac, title="recordings: backup failed",
                message="backup failed (BackupError; exit 1). See Status.")
    (req,) = ntfy.requests
    assert (req["method"], req["path"]) == ("POST", "/topic-do-not-print_1")
    assert req["headers"]["Title"] == "recordings: backup failed"
    assert (req["headers"]["Priority"], req["headers"]["Tags"]) == ("4", "warning")
    assert req["body"] == "backup failed (BackupError; exit 1). See Status."
    assert "Authorization" not in req["headers"]


def test_without_a_server_or_topic_nothing_is_sent(ntfy):
    assert not send(AlertConfig(ntfy.url, None, None), title="t", message="m")
    assert not send(AlertConfig(None, "topic", None), title="t", message="m")
    assert ntfy.requests == []


def test_a_failed_delivery_never_raises_and_never_logs_the_topic(ntfy, caplog):
    ntfy.status = 500
    ac = AlertConfig(ntfy_server=ntfy.url, topic="topic-do-not-print", deadman_url=None)
    with caplog.at_level("WARNING"):
        assert send(ac, title="recordings: check failed", message="m") is False
    with socket.socket() as s:  # a port with nothing listening
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        closed = f"http://127.0.0.1:{s.getsockname()[1]}"
    with caplog.at_level("WARNING"):
        assert send(AlertConfig(closed, "topic-do-not-print", None), title="t", message="m") is False
    assert "topic-do-not-print" not in caplog.text and "HTTP 500" in caplog.text


def test_the_dead_mans_switch_speaks_healthchecks(ntfy):
    # why: Healthchecks.io takes the URL alone as success, /start and /fail around a run, and /log
    # as a note that leaves the check's state alone (healthchecks.io/docs/http_api).
    ac = AlertConfig(None, None, f"{ntfy.url}/ping/abc-do-not-print/")
    assert ping_deadman(ac, "start") and ping_deadman(ac)
    assert ping_deadman(ac, "fail", message="backup failed (BackupError; exit 1). See Status.")
    assert ping_deadman(ac, "log", message="recordings alert-test")
    assert [(r["method"], r["path"]) for r in ntfy.requests] == [
        ("POST", "/ping/abc-do-not-print/start"), ("POST", "/ping/abc-do-not-print"),
        ("POST", "/ping/abc-do-not-print/fail"), ("POST", "/ping/abc-do-not-print/log")]
    assert ntfy.requests[2]["body"] == "backup failed (BackupError; exit 1). See Status."
    assert not ping_deadman(AlertConfig(None, None, None))


def test_the_config_reads_the_secrets_from_files_and_hides_them(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "topic").write_text("topic-do-not-print-20\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (tmp_path / "ping").write_text("https://hc.example/ping/do-not-print\n", encoding="utf-8")
    cfg_file = tmp_path / "config.toml"
    cfg_file.write_text('[alerts]\nntfy_server = "https://ntfy.sh/"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    environ = {"RECORDINGS_CONFIG": str(cfg_file),
               "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC_FILE": str(tmp_path / "topic"),
               "RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL_FILE": str(tmp_path / "ping")}
    ac = alerts.from_config(load_config(environ), environ)
    assert (ac.ntfy_server, ac.topic, ac.enabled) == (
        "https://ntfy.sh", "topic-do-not-print-20", True)
    assert "do-not-print" not in repr(ac) and "do-not-print" not in str(ac)
    for server in ("ntfy.sh", "http://ntfy.example"):
        cfg_file.write_text(f'[alerts]\nntfy_server = "{server}"\n', encoding="utf-8")
        with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="ntfy_server"):
            alerts.from_config(load_config(environ), environ)


def test_an_ntfy_token_goes_in_a_bearer_header_and_nowhere_else(tmp_path, ntfy):
    (tmp_path / "token").write_text("tk_do-not-print\n", encoding="utf-8")
    cfg_file = tmp_path / "config.toml"
    cfg_file.write_text(f'[alerts]\nntfy_server = "{ntfy.url}"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    environ = {"RECORDINGS_CONFIG": str(cfg_file), "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC": "alerts-topic",
               "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOKEN_FILE": str(tmp_path / "token")}
    ac = alerts.from_config(load_config(environ), environ)
    assert send(ac, title="recordings: test alert", message="m")
    assert ntfy.requests[0]["headers"]["Authorization"] == "Bearer tk_do-not-print"
    assert "do-not-print" not in repr(ac)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field, value", [
    ("ntfy_server", "ntfy.sh"),
    ("ntfy_server", "http://ntfy.example"),
    ("ntfy_server", "https://user:do-not-print@ntfy.example"),
    ("deadman_url", "http://hc-ping.example/do-not-print"),
    ("deadman_url", "hc-ping.com/do-not-print"),
    ("topic", "do-not-print/1"),
    ("topic", "x" * 65),
])
def test_plain_http_credentials_in_a_url_and_odd_topics_are_refused(field, value):
    # why: https keeps the topic and the ping URL's token off the wire in clear (security review);
    # ntfy topics are [-_A-Za-z0-9]{1,64} (ops review). The error never repeats the value.
    fields = {"ntfy_server": None, "topic": None, "deadman_url": None, field: value}
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError) as caught:
        AlertConfig(**fields)
    assert "do-not-print" not in str(caught.value) and "x" * 65 not in str(caught.value)
    AlertConfig("http://127.0.0.1:8080", "alerts-topic", "http://localhost:1/p")  # loopback is fine


@pytest.mark.parametrize("code", [301, 302, 303, 307, 308])
def test_a_redirect_is_never_followed_and_the_alert_is_not_delivered(
        ntfy, other_ntfy, caplog, code):
    # why: urlopen's default opener follows a 301, 302 or 303 answer to a POST as a GET, to any host
    # and even from https down to http, with the Authorization and Title headers (security review).
    # Here nothing may reach the second server, and a redirected alert is not a delivered one.
    ntfy.redirect, ntfy.redirect_code = other_ntfy.url, code
    ac = AlertConfig(ntfy.url, "alerts-topic", f"{ntfy.url}/ping/abc", token="tk_do-not-print")
    with caplog.at_level("WARNING"):
        assert send(ac, title="recordings: backup failed", message="m") is False
        assert ping_deadman(ac, "fail", message="m") is False
    assert len(ntfy.requests) == 2 and other_ntfy.requests == []
    assert f"HTTP {code}" in caplog.text and "do-not-print" not in caplog.text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field, value", [
    ("deadman_url", "https://hc-ping.example/key/do-not-print?create=1"),
    ("deadman_url", "https://hc-ping.example/do-not-print?"),
    ("deadman_url", "https://hc-ping.example/do-not-print#x"),
    ("ntfy_server", "https://ntfy.example/?do-not-print"),
    ("ntfy_server", "https://ntfy.example\tdo-not-print"),
    ("ntfy_server", "https://ntfy.example:do-not-print"),
    ("ntfy_server", "https://ntf\u0443.example/do-not-print"),
])
def test_a_url_whose_suffix_would_not_land_on_its_path_is_refused(field, value):
    # why: /start, /fail and the topic are added to the end of the URL. After a ? or a # they land
    # in the query or are dropped, and Healthchecks takes ".../slug?create=1/fail" as a plain
    # success ping, so every failed backup would keep the dead-man's switch quiet. A tab, which
    # urlsplit drops but the request keeps, a bad port and a look-alike non-ASCII host are refused
    # too (security council).
    fields = {"ntfy_server": None, "topic": None, "deadman_url": None, field: value}
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError) as caught:
        AlertConfig(**fields)
    assert "do-not-print" not in str(caught.value)


def test_a_topic_that_is_the_only_lock_is_long_and_a_token_is_one_visible_word():
    # why: on a public server such as ntfy.sh the topic is the password (ntfy.sh's terms): whoever
    # guesses it reads the alerts and can send false ones, such as "recovered". The runbook asks for
    # 20 or more random characters (security council).
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="20") as caught:
        AlertConfig("https://ntfy.sh", "do-not-print", None)
    assert "do-not-print" not in str(caught.value)
    AlertConfig("https://ntfy.sh", "x" * 20, None)
    AlertConfig("https://ntfy.example", "alerts", None, token="tk_abc")  # access control: a token
    AlertConfig("http://127.0.0.1:8080", "alerts", None)  # the tests' server on this machine
    for token in ("tk_a\r\n X-Folded: do-not-print", "tk do-not-print", "tk_\u00e9do-not-print"):
        with pytest.raises(ConfigError) as caught:
            AlertConfig("https://ntfy.example", "alerts", None, token=token)
        assert "do-not-print" not in str(caught.value)


def test_an_http_proxy_never_carries_an_alert_and_nothing_secret_is_logged(
        ntfy, other_ntfy, monkeypatch, caplog):
    # why: urllib sends plain http through HTTP_PROXY as the whole URL with every header, the topic,
    # the ping URL and the token in clear. Only an https proxy is used, and through it an alert
    # travels in a CONNECT tunnel that shows the proxy the host name alone (security council).
    for name in ("HTTP_PROXY", "http_proxy", "ALL_PROXY", "all_proxy"):
        monkeypatch.setenv(name, other_ntfy.url)
    for name in ("NO_PROXY", "no_proxy"):
        monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(alerts, "_OPENER", alerts._build_opener())
    ac = AlertConfig(ntfy.url, "topic-do-not-print", f"{ntfy.url}/ping/do-not-print",
                     token="tk_do-not-print")
    with caplog.at_level("DEBUG"):
        assert send(ac, title="recordings: test alert", message="m")
        assert ping_deadman(ac, "fail", message="m")
        ntfy.status = 404
        assert send(ac, title="recordings: test alert", message="m") is False
    assert other_ntfy.requests == [] and len(ntfy.requests) == 3
    assert "do-not-print" not in caplog.text
```

`packages/core/tests/test_ops.py`:
```python
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import subprocess
from contextlib import closing, contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from recordings import disk, ops
from recordings.cli import main
from recordings.config import load_config
from recordings.locks import Locks
from recordings.ops import Context, due, enabled_jobs, loop, run_due, run_job

T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 9, 8, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
SUMMARY = json.dumps({"message_type": "summary", "snapshot_id": "f" * 64,
                      "total_files_processed": 1, "data_added": 1})
TITLE = "会議メモ / Q&A"  # Review Focus 4: a synthetic non-ASCII title


class Clock:
    def __init__(self, now=T0):
        self.now = now

    def __call__(self):
        return self.now


def restic(returncode=0, stderr=""):
    def run(cmd, **kwargs):
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, returncode, SUMMARY if returncode == 0 else "", stderr)
    return run


def raising(exc):
    def run(cmd, **kwargs):
        raise exc
    return run


def context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, *, clock=None, runner=None, mirror=False):
    (tmp_path / "pw").write_text("pw\n", encoding="utf-8")
    deploy = tmp_path / "deploy.env"
    deploy.write_text("X=1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    mirror_section = f'[mirror]\ntarget = "{tmp_path / "mirror"}"\n' if mirror else ""
    cfg_file = tmp_path / "config.toml"
    cfg_file.write_text(
        f'[archive]\npath = "{writer.root}"\nwriter_id = "test"\n'
        f'[state]\npath = "{writer.state.path}"\n'
        f'[backup]\nrepository = "{tmp_path / "repo"}"\nextra_paths = ["{deploy}"]\n'
        f'restore_scratch = "{tmp_path / "scratch"}"\n'
        f'[alerts]\nntfy_server = "{ntfy.url}"\n{mirror_section}', encoding="utf-8")
    environ = {"RECORDINGS_CONFIG": str(cfg_file), "RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE": str(tmp_path / "pw"),
               "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC": "alerts-topic", "RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL": f"{ntfy.url}/ping",
               "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": str(tmp_path)}
    return Context(cfg=load_config(environ), environ=environ, state=writer.state,
                   clock=clock or Clock(), runner=runner or restic())


def own_environment(ctx, monkeypatch):
    """The process environment is the context's alone: a CLI command reads os.environ, and Dan's
    real RECORDINGS_* and RESTIC_* settings (a topic file, a token, a ping URL) must not get in."""
    for key in [k for k in os.environ if k.startswith(("RECORDINGS_", "RESTIC_"))]:
        monkeypatch.delenv(key)
    for key, value in ctx.environ.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(key, value)


def pushes(ntfy):
    """The ntfy alerts: POSTs to the topic."""
    return [r for r in ntfy.requests if r["path"] == "/alerts-topic"]


def pings(ntfy):
    """The dead-man's switch pings, by path."""
    return [r["path"] for r in ntfy.requests if r["path"].startswith("/ping")]


def test_which_jobs_run_comes_from_config(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    assert enabled_jobs(context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy).cfg) == (
        "disk", "backup", "prune", "check", "restore-test")
    assert "mirror" in enabled_jobs(context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, mirror=True).cfg)


def test_a_job_is_due_after_its_interval_and_a_failure_is_retried_after_15_minutes(writer):
    state = writer.state
    assert due(state, T0, ("backup", "check")) == ["backup", "check"]
    state.record_run("backup", T0, T0, True, "ok")
    assert due(state, T0 + timedelta(minutes=59), ("backup",)) == []
    assert due(state, T0 + timedelta(hours=1), ("backup",)) == ["backup"]
    later = T0 + timedelta(hours=2)
    state.record_run("backup", later, later, False, "failed")
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(minutes=14), ("backup",)) == []
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(minutes=15), ("backup",)) == ["backup"]
    # why: a failed restore test restores the whole archive again, and a failed check reads a
    # quarter of the repository: once a day, not every 15 minutes (Task 11's ops council)
    state.record_run("restore-test", later, later, False, "RestoreTestFailed")
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(hours=23), ("restore-test",)) == []
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(hours=24), ("restore-test",)) == ["restore-test"]
    # why: a failed mirror walks both trees twice to fail again, and one short of space first
    # reads and rewrites all it staged: its own hour, not every 15 minutes (Task 12's ops council)
    state.record_run("mirror", later, later, False, "MirrorError; exit 11")
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(minutes=59), ("mirror",)) == []
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(hours=1), ("mirror",)) == ["mirror"]
    # why: one run stamped in the future, by a clock that ran ahead, must not hold every job
    # back until the clock catches up with it
    ahead = T0 + timedelta(days=400)
    state.record_run("backup", ahead, ahead, True, "ok")
    state.record_run("check", ahead, ahead, False, "BackupError; exit 1")
    assert due(state, later + timedelta(hours=1), ("backup", "check")) == ["backup", "check"]


def test_a_good_backup_pings_the_dead_mans_switch(tmp_path, writer, make_incoming, ntfy):
    writer.add(make_incoming())
    assert run_job(context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy), "backup").ok
    assert pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/start", "/ping"] and pushes(ntfy) == []


def test_a_killed_backup_alerts_once_reminds_daily_and_says_when_it_recovers(
        tmp_path, writer, make_incoming, ntfy):
    # why: §20, "a killed backup raises an alert". A killed restic exits -9.
    writer.add(make_incoming())
    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock, runner=restic(returncode=-9))
    result = run_job(ctx, "backup")
    assert (result.ok, result.detail) == (False, "BackupError; exit -9")
    clock.now += timedelta(hours=1)
    run_job(ctx, "backup")  # still failing: no second alert yet
    clock.now += timedelta(hours=24)
    run_job(ctx, "backup")  # a reminder
    ctx.runner = restic()
    clock.now += timedelta(hours=1)
    assert run_job(ctx, "backup").ok
    assert [(r["headers"]["Title"], r["body"]) for r in pushes(ntfy)] == [
        ("recordings: backup failed", "backup failed (BackupError; exit -9). See Status."),
        ("recordings: backup failed", "backup failed (BackupError; exit -9). See Status."),
        ("recordings: backup recovered", "backup works again. See Status.")]
    assert pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/start", "/ping/fail"] * 3 + ["/ping/start", "/ping"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("runner, detail", [
    (restic(returncode=1, stderr=f"Fatal: open /archive/recordings/2026/10/x/{TITLE}.md: "
                                 "permission denied\n"), "BackupError; exit 1"),
    (raising(PermissionError(13, "Permission denied", f"/archive/{TITLE}.md")), "PermissionError"),
], ids=["restic-stderr", "oserror-path"])
def test_no_alert_or_stored_run_carries_an_exceptions_text(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, caplog, runner, detail):
    # why: Review Focus 4. An exception's text can hold a title, a path or a tool's own output.
    # Alerts go to third parties (ntfy.sh, Healthchecks.io), and Status shows the stored detail.
    # Only the container's debug log may carry the full text.
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, runner=runner)
    with caplog.at_level("INFO"):
        result = run_job(ctx, "backup")
    assert (result.ok, result.detail) == (False, detail)
    assert len(pushes(ntfy)) == 1 and pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/start", "/ping/fail"]
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(writer.state.db_path)) as db:
        stored = "\n".join(db.iterdump())
    sent = json.dumps(ntfy.requests, ensure_ascii=False)
    for text in (stored, sent, caplog.text):
        assert "会議" not in text


def test_low_disk_space_raises_an_alert(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    monkeypatch.setattr(disk.os, "statvfs", lambda p: SimpleNamespace(
        f_bavail=150, f_frsize=1024, f_blocks=1000))
    result = run_job(context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy), "disk")
    assert (result.ok, result.detail) == (False, "DiskWarning")
    (req,) = pushes(ntfy)
    assert req["headers"]["Title"] == "recordings: disk space low"
    assert req["body"] == "disk failed (DiskWarning). See Status."
    assert pings(ntfy) == []  # only a backup pings the dead-man's switch


def test_run_due_runs_what_is_due_and_beats_the_heart(tmp_path, writer, make_incoming, ntfy):
    writer.add(make_incoming())
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    results = {r.job for r in run_due(ctx)}
    assert {"disk", "backup", "prune", "check"} <= results
    assert writer.state.meta("ops_heartbeat") == T0.isoformat()
    assert writer.state.meta("ops_runs_trimmed") == T0.isoformat()  # the daily trim ran too
    assert {r.job for r in run_due(ctx)} <= {"restore-test"}  # the rest ran a moment ago


def test_a_busy_ops_lock_skips_quietly(tmp_path, writer, make_incoming, ntfy):
    # why: the CLI and the loop share one flock in /state (ops review). The loop never waits, and
    # a skip is not a failure: nothing is recorded, alerted or pinged, and the next tick retries.
    writer.add(make_incoming())
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    with Locks(writer.state.locks_dir, timeout=0).hold("ops"):
        results = run_due(ctx)
        assert results and all((r.ok, r.detail) == (False, "skipped: busy") for r in results)
        assert run_job(ctx, "backup", lock_timeout=0.2).detail == "skipped: busy"
    assert ntfy.requests == [] and writer.state.last_run("backup") is None
    assert "backup" in {r.job for r in run_due(ctx) if r.ok}  # free again: it runs


def test_an_unopenable_lock_file_or_state_is_a_recorded_failure_not_a_crash(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: run_job replaces Task 11's, whose lock-file handling must survive: an OSError opening
    # the lock (permissions, a full disk) escaping here would crash the backup service on a loop.
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)

    class Unopenable:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            pass

        def hold(self, key):
            raise PermissionError(13, "Permission denied")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "Locks", Unopenable)
    assert run_job(ctx, "check") == ops.JobResult("check", False, "PermissionError")
    assert writer.state.last_run("check").detail == "PermissionError"
    assert all(not r.ok for r in run_due(ctx))  # and the loop's pass returns normally
    monkeypatch.undo()

    def broken(*args, **kwargs):
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError("disk I/O error")

    monkeypatch.setattr(writer.state, "record_run", broken)
    assert run_job(ctx, "check").ok  # a state disk that can't record must not turn into a crash


def test_a_state_disk_that_cannot_write_or_read_never_stops_a_job_an_alert_or_the_loop(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: a broken state.db reached the loop three more ways than record_run: the alert state's
    # read and write, the heartbeat, and due()'s own reads. None may end the backup service.
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, runner=restic(returncode=1))

    def broken(*args, **kwargs):
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError("disk I/O error")

    for name in ("record_run", "alert_state", "set_alert_state", "set_meta"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(writer.state, name, broken)
    result = run_job(ctx, "backup")
    assert (result.ok, result.detail) == (False, "BackupError; exit 1")
    assert len(pushes(ntfy)) == 1 and pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/start", "/ping/fail"]  # still said
    ctx.runner = restic()
    assert run_job(ctx, "backup").ok  # and a good run returns, with no recovery it can know of
    assert all(isinstance(r, ops.JobResult) for r in run_due(ctx))  # the heartbeat write fails too
    monkeypatch.setattr(writer.state, "last_run", broken)  # due() cannot read either
    ticks = []
    loop(ctx, tick=0, sleep=lambda s: ticks.append(s), stop=lambda: len(ticks) >= 2)
    assert len(ticks) == 2


def test_old_runs_are_trimmed_daily_but_each_jobs_newest_good_run_stays(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    # why: ops_runs gets about 70,000 rows a year. Status must still know a job's last good run
    # after a long failing streak, so that row is kept however old it is.
    state = writer.state
    old = T0 - timedelta(days=200)
    state.record_run("backup", old, old, True, "snapshot a")                   # newest good: kept
    state.record_run("check", old, old, True, "old good, superseded")           # dropped
    state.record_run("check", old + timedelta(days=1), old + timedelta(days=1), True, "kept")
    for day in range(2, 150):                                                  # a failing streak
        at = old + timedelta(days=day)
        state.record_run("backup", at, at, False, "BackupError; exit 1")
    recent = T0 - timedelta(days=3)
    state.record_run("disk", recent, recent, True, "ok")
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    ops._trim_runs(ctx)
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(state.db_path)) as db:
        kept = db.execute("SELECT job, ok, detail FROM ops_runs ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    assert ("backup", 1, "snapshot a") in kept and ("check", 1, "kept") in kept
    assert ("check", 1, "old good, superseded") not in kept
    # the streak's days 2 to 149 finished 198 to 51 days before T0: those inside 90 days stay
    assert sum(1 for r in kept if r[0] == "backup" and r[1] == 0) == 40
    assert state.last_run("backup", ok=True).detail == "snapshot a"
    assert state.meta("ops_runs_trimmed") == T0.isoformat()
    state.record_run("disk", old, old, True, "ancient")  # superseded below, so it may go
    state.record_run("disk", recent, recent, True, "ok")
    ctx.clock.now += timedelta(hours=1)
    ops._trim_runs(ctx)  # not again within a day
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(state.db_path)) as db:
        assert db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops_runs WHERE detail = 'ancient'").fetchone()[0] == 1
    ctx.clock.now += timedelta(days=1)
    ops._trim_runs(ctx)
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(state.db_path)) as db:
        assert db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops_runs WHERE detail = 'ancient'").fetchone()[0] == 0


def test_only_restics_exit_11_is_busy_rsyncs_is_a_failure(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: rsync's exit 11 is a file I/O error. Only a BackupError with restic's 11 is "locked".
    from recordings.mirror import MirrorError
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, mirror=True)

    def rsync_io_error(ctx, tags):
        raise MirrorError("rsync failed", returncode=11)

    monkeypatch.setitem(ops.JOBS, "mirror", rsync_io_error)
    result = run_job(ctx, "mirror", lock_timeout=0)
    assert (result.ok, result.detail) == (False, "MirrorError; exit 11")
    assert writer.state.last_run("mirror").detail == "MirrorError; exit 11"
    assert [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)] == ["recordings: mirror failed"]


def test_a_locked_repository_is_busy_not_a_failure(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    # why: the NAS's weekly forget --prune holds restic's lock (exit 11). That is not an outage.
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy,
                  runner=restic(11, "Fatal: repository is already locked exclusively"))
    result = run_job(ctx, "backup", lock_timeout=0)
    assert result.detail == "skipped: busy (repository locked)" and not result.ok
    assert writer.state.last_run("backup") is None and pushes(ntfy) == []
    assert pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/start"]  # started, never finished: the dead-man's switch decides


def test_the_loop_runs_until_told_to_stop(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    ticks = []
    loop(ctx, tick=0, sleep=lambda s: ticks.append(s), stop=lambda: len(ticks) >= 3)
    assert len(ticks) == 3


def test_the_loop_runs_with_sigterm_forwarded(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: the loop is PID 1 in its container, where SIGTERM does nothing without a handler, and
    # Docker would wait out stop_grace_period, then kill restic mid-run and leave its lock behind.
    # Inside sigterm_forwarded (Task 11), restic gets the SIGTERM, then the loop stops.
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    own_environment(ctx, monkeypatch)
    events = []

    @contextmanager
    def forwarded():
        events.append("forwarding")
        yield
        events.append("restored")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "sigterm_forwarded", forwarded)
    # the CLI waits for restic's lock (5m); the loop never does (§15.1): it is None by then
    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "loop", lambda ctx, **kwargs: events.append(
        f"loop retry_lock={ctx.retry_lock}"))
    assert main(["ops", "--loop"]) == 0
    assert events == ["forwarding", "loop retry_lock=None", "restored"]


def test_alert_test_sends_one_logs_the_check_and_never_prints_the_topic(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch, capsys):
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    own_environment(ctx, monkeypatch)
    assert main(["alert-test", "--json"]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert json.loads(out) == {"ntfy": True, "deadman": True}
    assert "alerts-topic" not in out
    assert [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)] == ["recordings: test alert"]
    assert pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/log"]  # /log: the check's state stays as it is


def test_alert_test_can_test_the_dead_mans_switch_alone_and_fails_when_a_ping_fails(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch, capsys):
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    own_environment(ctx, monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.delenv("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC")
    assert main(["alert-test", "--json"]) == 0  # no topic: ntfy is skipped, not failed
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == {"ntfy": None, "deadman": True}
    assert pushes(ntfy) == [] and pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/log"]
    monkeypatch.setenv("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC", "alerts-topic")
    ntfy.status = 500
    assert main(["alert-test", "--json"]) == 1
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == {"ntfy": False, "deadman": False}
    monkeypatch.delenv("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC")  # a failing ping alone fails the command
    assert main(["alert-test", "--json"]) == 1
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == {"ntfy": None, "deadman": False}
    monkeypatch.delenv("RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL")
    assert main(["alert-test", "--json"]) == 78  # nothing to test


def test_one_pass_of_ops_exits_75_when_every_turn_was_busy(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: `recordings backup` exits 75 (try again) on a busy turn, and so does a pass of ops
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    own_environment(ctx, monkeypatch)
    with Locks(writer.state.locks_dir, timeout=0).hold("ops"):
        assert main(["ops", "--json"]) == 75
    assert main(["ops", "--json"]) in (0, 1)  # free again: it ran


def test_a_full_state_disk_alerts_once_not_every_minute(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: a state.db that reads but can't write (a full disk) left every failing job due at every
    # tick and its alert unsaved: one push a minute until ntfy.sh refused them all (Task 13 review).
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    monkeypatch.setattr(disk.os, "statvfs", lambda p: SimpleNamespace(
        f_bavail=0, f_frsize=1024, f_blocks=1000))
    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock)

    def full(*args, **kwargs):
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError("database or disk is full")

    for name in ("record_run", "set_alert_state", "set_meta", "prune_runs"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(writer.state, name, full)
    run_due(ctx)
    titles = [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)]
    assert titles.count("recordings: disk space low") == 1
    sent, pinged = len(ntfy.requests), pings(ntfy)
    for _ in range(30):  # past RETRY_AFTER (15 min), so the alert memory is what holds, not only the attempts
        clock.now += timedelta(minutes=1)
        run_due(ctx)
    assert [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)] == titles
    assert len(ntfy.requests) == sent and pings(ntfy) == pinged  # no job ran again either


def test_a_locked_repository_is_not_retried_every_minute(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    # why: a locked repository is not recorded, so every tick of the NAS's retention run brought
    # ssh, a state.db copy, restic unlock and restic backup again (Task 13 review).
    calls = []

    def locked(cmd, **kwargs):
        calls.append(cmd)
        return restic(11, "Fatal: repository is already locked exclusively")(cmd, **kwargs)

    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock, runner=locked)
    run_due(ctx)
    first = len(calls)
    assert first
    clock.now += timedelta(minutes=1)
    run_due(ctx)
    assert len(calls) == first
    clock.now += ops.RETRY_AFTER
    run_due(ctx)
    assert len(calls) > first


def test_a_job_that_raises_anything_is_a_failure_and_the_loop_carries_on(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: only FAILURES were caught, so a bug in one job ended the loop, and on restart the same
    # unrecorded job was due first again and the jobs after it never ran (Task 13 review).
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)

    def bug(ctx, tags):
        raise KeyError(TITLE)

    monkeypatch.setitem(ops.JOBS, "check", bug)
    results = {r.job: r for r in run_due(ctx)}
    assert (results["check"].ok, results["check"].detail) == (False, "KeyError")
    assert "restore-test" in results  # the jobs after it still ran
    assert writer.state.last_run("check").detail == "KeyError"
    assert "recordings: backup check failed" in [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)]
    assert "会議" not in json.dumps(ntfy.requests, ensure_ascii=False)


def test_the_loop_logs_a_fixed_line_and_keeps_the_traceback_for_debug(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch, caplog):
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)

    def broken(*args, **kwargs):
        raise ValueError(TITLE)

    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "due", broken)
    ticks = []
    with caplog.at_level("INFO"):
        loop(ctx, tick=0, sleep=lambda s: ticks.append(s), stop=lambda: len(ticks) >= 1)
    warnings = [r for r in caplog.records if r.levelname == "WARNING"]
    assert warnings and all(r.exc_info is None for r in warnings)
    assert "ValueError" in caplog.text and "会議" not in caplog.text


def test_an_unopenable_lock_file_alerts_and_a_backup_pings_fail(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: §14, a failed backup raises an alert. This failure was recorded but never said, so only
    # the dead-man's switch noticed, after its period and grace.
    class Unopenable:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            pass

        def hold(self, key):
            raise PermissionError(13, "Permission denied")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "Locks", Unopenable)
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy)
    assert run_job(ctx, "backup") == ops.JobResult("backup", False, "PermissionError")
    assert [r["headers"]["Title"] for r in pushes(ntfy)] == ["recordings: backup failed"]
    assert pings(ntfy) == ["/ping/fail"]

    writer.state.set_alert_state("job:backup", failing=True,
                                 last_sent_at=T0 + timedelta(days=400))  # a clock that ran ahead
    run_job(context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, runner=restic(returncode=1)), "backup")
    assert len(pushes(ntfy)) == 1


def test_an_undelivered_alert_is_sent_again_at_the_next_failure(tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
    # why: a refused push must not count as sent, or nothing is said for the next 24 hours
    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock, runner=restic(returncode=1))
    ntfy.status = 500
    run_job(ctx, "backup")
    ntfy.status = 200
    clock.now += timedelta(hours=1)
    run_job(ctx, "backup")
    assert len(pushes(ntfy)) == 2
    clock.now += timedelta(hours=1)
    run_job(ctx, "backup")  # delivered at last: now quiet until the daily reminder
    assert len(pushes(ntfy)) == 2

        tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: the disk job shared one alert state between a low disk and a missing marker, so the
    # flip from one to the other waited for the daily reminder (Task 13 re-review)
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    monkeypatch.setattr(disk.os, "statvfs", lambda p: SimpleNamespace(
        f_bavail=0, f_frsize=1024, f_blocks=1000))
    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock)
    run_job(ctx, "disk")
    real_uuid = writer.state.meta("archive_uuid")

    clock.now += timedelta(minutes=20)

def test_a_future_stamp_and_a_full_state_disk_still_alert_once(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, monkeypatch):
    # why: a run and an alert row stamped in the future (a clock that ran ahead, then was put
    # right) were taken as newer than the process's own memory, so a full state disk brought back
    # a push a minute (Task 13 re-review)
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    monkeypatch.setattr(disk.os, "statvfs", lambda p: SimpleNamespace(
        f_bavail=0, f_frsize=1024, f_blocks=1000))
    future = T0 + timedelta(days=2)
    writer.state.record_run("disk", future - timedelta(minutes=1), future, False, "DiskWarning")
    writer.state.set_alert_state("job:disk", failing=True, last_sent_at=future)
    clock = Clock()
    ctx = context(tmp_path, writer, ntfy, clock=clock)

    def full(*args, **kwargs):
        raise sqlite3.OperationalError("database or disk is full")

    for name in ("record_run", "set_alert_state", "set_meta", "prune_runs"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(writer.state, name, full)
    runs = 0
    for _ in range(31):
        runs += sum(r.job == "disk" for r in run_due(ctx))
        clock.now += timedelta(minutes=1)
    assert runs == 3  # minutes 0, 15 and 30: a future stamp must not make the job due every minute
    assert len([r for r in pushes(ntfy) if r["body"].startswith("disk failed")]) == 1


def test_a_marker_failure_that_recovers_alone_is_cleared_and_said_again_when_it_returns(
        tmp_path, writer, ntfy):
```

In `packages/core/src/recordings/config.py`, **add** to `SECRETS`:

```python
        "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC", "the private ntfy topic that alerts go to", 2),
    "deadman_url": SecretSpec(
        "RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL", "the Healthchecks.io ping URL (it carries its own token)", 2),

        "RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOKEN", "an ntfy access token, only for a server that needs one", 2,

```

`packages/core/src/recordings/alerts.py`:
```python
"""Alerts (spec §14): push notifications through ntfy, and a dead-man's switch.

- **ntfy** (https://docs.ntfy.sh/publish/): a POST to <server>/<topic>, with the message as the
  body and Title, Priority and Tags headers. The topic is a secret, because anyone who knows it
  can read the alerts. It is never logged, printed, or put in an error. A server that needs an
  access token gets one as `Authorization: Bearer` (RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOKEN_FILE); ntfy.sh needs
  none.
- **The dead-man's switch** is a Healthchecks.io check (https://healthchecks.io/docs/http_api/).
  Each backup pings <url>/start, then <url> when it worked or <url>/fail when it didn't.
  `recordings alert-test` pings <url>/log, which leaves the check's state alone. Healthchecks
  alerts when the pings stop, and that is what notices a stopped container or a dead server. Its
  period is 1 hour and its grace at least 3 hours, because the loop runs one job at a time and a
  long check or restore test holds back the next backup (docs/runbooks/first-run.md).

Both URLs must be https, so the topic, the token and the ping URL never cross a network in clear;
plain http is allowed only to this machine's loopback (the tests' fake server). Neither may hold a
query or a fragment, since /start, /fail and the topic are added to its end. A redirect is never
followed, because it would carry the token and the title to another host, and only an https proxy
is used: a CONNECT tunnel shows it the host name alone. Without a token the topic is the alerts'
only lock (ntfy.sh's topics are public), so it is at least MIN_OPEN_TOPIC long. Alert text comes
from fixed templates (a job, an exception's class, an exit code), never a recording's title, a
path or a tool's own output (Review Focus 4). Sending never raises: a failed delivery is logged
without its URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import http.client
import logging
import re
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from recordings import __version__
from recordings.config import Config, ConfigError, secret

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
TIMEOUT = 10.0
TOPIC_RE = re.compile(r"[-_A-Za-z0-9]{1,64}")
MIN_OPEN_TOPIC = 20  # without a token: the runbook's "20 or more random letters and digits"
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[!-~]{1,256}")  # visible ASCII, one word: nothing folded into a header
PINGS = {"success": "", "start": "/start", "fail": "/fail", "log": "/log"}
_LOOPBACK = frozenset({"127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost"})


class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    """urlopen follows a 301, 302 or 303 answer to a POST as a GET to any host, even from https down
    to http, with the Authorization and Title headers: an alert is never redirected."""

    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None  # HTTPDefaultErrorHandler raises HTTPError(code): logged, not delivered


def _build_opener() -> urllib.request.OpenerDirector:
    """Proxies from the environment only, and only for https: through one, an alert travels in a
    CONNECT tunnel, and the proxy sees the host name, never the topic, the token or the ping URL.
    Plain http (the loopback) never goes to a proxy, which would get the whole request in clear.
    The default handler would also ask macOS's system configuration, which starts threads that
    never end (and makes a later fork() warn)."""
    proxies = urllib.request.getproxies_environment()
    return urllib.request.build_opener(
        urllib.request.ProxyHandler({k: v for k, v in proxies.items() if k == "https"}),
        _NoRedirect)


_OPENER = _build_opener()


def _check_url(url: object, what: str) -> None:
    """https, with a host and no user name or password in it; http only to the loopback. No query
    or fragment: after a ? or a #, the /fail or the topic added to the end would land in the query
    (Healthchecks takes it as a plain success ping) or be dropped. Visible ASCII only, so the URL
    checked is the URL sent (urlsplit drops a tab or a newline the request keeps) and a host can't
    be a look-alike. The error names the setting, never the URL, which may be a secret."""
    plain = isinstance(url, str) and url.isascii() and url.isprintable() and not any(
        c in url for c in " ?#")
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(url) if plain else None
        host = parts.hostname if parts else None
        _ = parts.port if parts else None  # a port that isn't a number raises ValueError
    except ValueError:  # a malformed IPv6 address, or port
        parts, host = None, None
    if parts is None or not host or "@" in parts.netloc or not (
            parts.scheme == "https" or (parts.scheme == "http" and host in _LOOPBACK)):
        raise ConfigError(f"{what} must be an https:// URL in plain ASCII, with no user name, "
                          "password, query (?) or fragment (#) in it")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AlertConfig:
    ntfy_server: str | None
    topic: str | None
    deadman_url: str | None
    token: str | None = None  # an ntfy access token, for a server that needs one

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.ntfy_server is not None:
            _check_url(self.ntfy_server, "[alerts] ntfy_server")
        if self.deadman_url is not None:
            _check_url(self.deadman_url, "RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL")
        if self.topic is not None and not TOPIC_RE.fullmatch(self.topic):
            raise ConfigError("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC must be 1 to 64 letters, digits, '-' or '_'")
        if self.token is not None and not TOKEN_RE.fullmatch(self.token):
            raise ConfigError("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOKEN must be one word of visible ASCII")
        if (self.topic is not None and self.token is None and self.ntfy_server is not None
                and urlsplit(self.ntfy_server).hostname not in _LOOPBACK
                and len(self.topic) < MIN_OPEN_TOPIC):
            raise ConfigError(f"RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC must be {MIN_OPEN_TOPIC} or more random "
                              "characters: with no token, it is all that keeps the alerts private")

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.ntfy_server and self.topic)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # never the topic, the ping URL or the token
        return (f"AlertConfig(ntfy_server={self.ntfy_server!r}, "
                f"topic={'set' if self.topic else None}, "
                f"deadman_url={'set' if self.deadman_url else None}, "
                f"token={'set' if self.token else None})")

    __str__ = __repr__


def from_config(cfg: Config, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> AlertConfig:
    server = cfg.data.get("alerts", {}).get("ntfy_server")
    return AlertConfig(ntfy_server=server.rstrip("/") if isinstance(server, str) else server,
                       topic=secret("ntfy_topic", environ),
                       deadman_url=secret("deadman_url", environ),
                       token=secret("ntfy_token", environ))


def _deliver(request: urllib.request.Request) -> bool:
    try:
        with _OPENER.open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            return 200 <= response.status < 300
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        log.warning("delivery failed: HTTP %s", exc.code)
        exc.close()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, http.client.HTTPException, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        log.warning("delivery failed: %s", type(exc).__name__)
    return False


def send(ac: AlertConfig, *, title: str, message: str, priority: int = 4,
         tags: Sequence[str] = ("warning",)) -> bool:
    """Push one alert. The title and the message come from fixed templates (Review Focus 4)."""
    if not ac.enabled:
        return False
    headers = {"Title": title, "Priority": str(priority), "Tags": ",".join(tags),
               "User-Agent": f"recordings/{__version__}"}
    if ac.token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {ac.token}"
    delivered = _deliver(urllib.request.Request(
        f"{ac.ntfy_server}/{ac.topic}", data=message.encode("utf-8"), method="POST",
        headers=headers))
    if not delivered:
        log.warning("alert %r was not delivered", title)
    return delivered


def ping_deadman(ac: AlertConfig, kind: str = "success", *, message: str = "") -> bool:
    """One Healthchecks ping, `kind` being a key of PINGS. The body is a fixed text."""
    if not ac.deadman_url:
        return False
    return _deliver(urllib.request.Request(
        ac.deadman_url.rstrip("/") + PINGS[kind], data=message.encode("utf-8"), method="POST",
        headers={"User-Agent": f"recordings/{__version__}"}))
```

```python
    # ---- alert state: one alert per failure, a daily reminder, and "recovered" ---------------
    def alert_state(self, key: str) -> tuple[bool, datetime | None]:
        with self.db() as db:
            row = db.execute("SELECT failing, last_sent_at FROM alerts WHERE key = ?",
                             (key,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return False, None
        return bool(row[0]), datetime.fromisoformat(row[1]) if row[1] else None

    def set_alert_state(self, key: str, *, failing: bool, last_sent_at: datetime | None) -> None:
        with self.db() as db:
            db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO alerts (key, failing, last_sent_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                       (key, int(failing), last_sent_at.isoformat() if last_sent_at else None))

    # ---- ops_runs retention: the loop trims it once a day (ops._trim_runs) ---------------------
    def prune_runs(self, before: datetime) -> int:
        """Delete the runs that finished before `before`, except each job's newest run and its
        newest good one (what Status and the schedule read, however long a job has been failing).
        Returns how many rows went."""
        with self.db() as db:
            return db.execute(
                "DELETE FROM ops_runs WHERE datetime(finished_at) < datetime(?) "
                "AND id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM ops_runs WHERE ok = 1 GROUP BY job) "
                "AND id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM ops_runs GROUP BY job)",
                (before.isoformat(),)).rowcount
```

   ```python
   INTERVALS = {"disk": timedelta(minutes=10), "backup": timedelta(hours=1),
                "mirror": timedelta(hours=1), "prune": timedelta(days=1),
                "check": timedelta(days=7), "restore-test": timedelta(days=30)}
   ORDER = ("disk", "backup", "mirror", "prune", "check", "restore-test")
   RETRY_AFTER = timedelta(minutes=15)
   # A failed check reads a quarter of the repository again, and a failed restore test all of it,
   # for hours in which the loop does nothing else: once a day is enough, and the alert has said
   # it failed. (Task 11's ops council.) A failed mirror walks both trees twice to fail again, and
   # one short of space first reads and rewrites all it staged: its own hour is soon enough.
   # (Task 12's ops council)
   RETRY_HEAVY_AFTER = {"check": timedelta(hours=24), "restore-test": timedelta(hours=24),
                        "mirror": timedelta(hours=1)}
   REMIND_EVERY = timedelta(hours=24)
   KEEP_RUNS = timedelta(days=90)  # ops_runs gets about 70,000 rows a year; older ones go, daily
   PRUNE_RUNS_EVERY = timedelta(days=1)
   REPO_LOCKED = 11  # restic's exit status for a repository another process holds (the NAS's retention)
   LOCKED = f"{BUSY} (repository locked)"
   TITLES = {"disk": "disk space low", "backup": "backup failed", "mirror": "mirror failed",
             "prune": "backup retention failed", "check": "backup check failed",
             "restore-test": "restore test failed"}
   DETAIL_TITLES = {"ArchiveMarkerError": "archive disk missing or changed"}  # a failure of its own kind


   def enabled_jobs(cfg: Config) -> tuple[str, ...]:
       jobs = {"disk"}
       if cfg.data.get("backup", {}).get("repository"):
           jobs |= {"backup", "prune", "check", "restore-test"}
       if cfg.data.get("mirror", {}).get("target"):
           jobs.add("mirror")
       return tuple(j for j in ORDER if j in jobs)


   def due(state: State, now: datetime, jobs: tuple[str, ...],
           attempts: Mapping[str, tuple[datetime, bool]] | None = None) -> list[str]:
       """A run stamped in the future (a clock that ran ahead and was put right) counts as long
       ago: otherwise every job, backups included, would wait for the clock to catch up. `attempts`
       are the runs this process could not record (a full state disk): one newer than state.db's
       counts as the job's latest run, so a failing job waits its retry rather than running at
       every tick."""
       out = []
       for job in jobs:
           last, good = state.last_run(job), state.last_run(job, ok=True)
           last_at, last_ok = (last.finished_at, last.ok) if last is not None else (None, True)
           good_at = good.finished_at if good is not None else None
           tried = (attempts or {}).get(job)
           if tried is not None and (last_at is None or tried[0] > last_at or last_at > now):
               last_at, last_ok = tried
               if last_ok:
                   good_at = last_at
           wait = RETRY_HEAVY_AFTER.get(job, RETRY_AFTER)
           if last_at is not None and not last_ok and timedelta(0) <= now - last_at < wait:
               continue
           if good_at is None or not timedelta(0) <= now - good_at < INTERVALS[job]:
               out.append(job)
       return out


   def _alert_config(ctx: Context) -> AlertConfig | None:
       try:
           return alerts.from_config(ctx.cfg, ctx.environ)
       except ConfigError as exc:  # its text names a setting, never a secret's value
           log.warning("alerts are not configured: %s", exc)
           return None


   def _alert(ctx: Context, ac: AlertConfig, job: str, ok: bool, detail: str) -> None:
       """One push when a job starts failing, a reminder every day while it fails, and one when it
       works again. The text is a fixed template: the job, the failure's fixed detail and "See
       Status", never a path, a title or a tool's own output (Review Focus 4). A state.db that
       can't be read or written never stops this, nor makes it say the same thing at every tick:
       the process keeps what it sent (ctx.alerted) for as long as it is newer than state.db's.
       A failure with a title of its own (DETAIL_TITLES) has an alert state of its own, so a flip to
       it is said at once, and one recovery clears them all."""
       now = ctx.clock()
       if ok:
           keys = [f"job:{job}", *(f"job:{job}:{kind}" for kind in DETAIL_TITLES)]
           failing = [key for key in keys if _known(ctx, key)[0]]
           if failing:
               alerts.send(ac, title=f"recordings: {job} recovered",
                           message=f"{job} works again. See Status.", priority=3,
                           tags=("white_check_mark",))
           for key in failing:
               _remember(ctx, key, failing=False, last_sent_at=now)
           return
       key = f"job:{job}:{detail}" if detail in DETAIL_TITLES else f"job:{job}"
       failing, last_sent = _known(ctx, key)
       if not failing or last_sent is None or not timedelta(0) <= now - last_sent < REMIND_EVERY:
           delivered = alerts.send(ac, title=f"recordings: {DETAIL_TITLES.get(detail, TITLES[job])}",
                                   message=f"{job} failed ({detail}). See Status.")
           last_sent = now if delivered else last_sent
       _remember(ctx, key, failing=True, last_sent_at=last_sent)


   def _known(ctx: Context, key: str) -> tuple[bool, datetime | None]:
       """What is known of one alert: state.db's row, or this process's own memory of it when that is
       newer, or when state.db can't be read."""
       mine = ctx.alerted.get(key)
       try:
           saved = ctx.state.alert_state(key)
       except FAILURES:  # state.db unreadable: the process's memory, or nothing sent so far
           log.warning("%s: could not read the alert state", key)
           saved = None
       if saved is None:
           return mine or (False, None)
       if mine is None:
           return saved
       newer = (saved[1] is not None and saved[1] <= ctx.clock()
                and (mine[1] is None or saved[1] > mine[1]))
       return saved if newer else mine


   def _remember(ctx: Context, key: str, *, failing: bool, last_sent_at: datetime | None) -> None:
       ctx.alerted[key] = (failing, last_sent_at)
       try:
           ctx.state.set_alert_state(key, failing=failing, last_sent_at=last_sent_at)
       except FAILURES:  # nothing to lose but the next reminder's timing
           log.warning("%s: could not save the alert state", key)


   def _conclude(ctx: Context, ac: AlertConfig | None, job: str, started: datetime, ok: bool,
                 detail: str) -> JobResult:
       """Record a run, alert, and for a backup ping the dead-man's switch: the URL itself or /fail.
       A state.db that can't record it leaves the attempt in ctx.attempts, for due()."""
       try:
           ctx.state.record_run(job, started, ctx.clock(), ok, detail)
       except FAILURES:  # a broken state disk must not hide the alert below (which guards its own)
           log.warning("%s: could not record the run (%s)", job, detail)
           ctx.attempts[job] = (ctx.clock(), ok)
       if ac is not None:
           _alert(ctx, ac, job, ok, detail)
           if job == "backup":
               alerts.ping_deadman(ac, "success" if ok else "fail",
                                   message="" if ok else f"{job} failed ({detail}). See Status.")
       return JobResult(job, ok, detail)


   def _run_held(ctx: Context, job: str, tags: tuple[str, ...]) -> JobResult:
       ac = _alert_config(ctx)
       if ac is not None and job == "backup":
           alerts.ping_deadman(ac, "start")
       started = ctx.clock()
       try:
           detail, ok = JOBS[job](ctx, tags), True
       except Exception as exc:  # any error is the job's failure: it must not end the loop
           if isinstance(exc, BackupError) and exc.returncode == REPO_LOCKED:
               # The NAS's weekly forget --prune holds the repository for a while. Not a failure:
               # not recorded, not alerted, no /fail ping. A backup that stays blocked leaves its
               # /start unanswered, and the dead-man's switch alerts after its grace. The loop
               # leaves the job alone for RETRY_AFTER (run_due).
               log.info("%s: %s", job, LOCKED)
               ctx.locked[job] = ctx.clock()
               return JobResult(job, False, LOCKED)
           log.debug("%s failed", job, exc_info=True)  # the full error, for --debug only
           detail, ok = failure_detail(exc), False
       return _conclude(ctx, ac, job, started, ok, detail)
   ```
5. **Replace** `run_job` (Task 11's, with its ops lock and the same signature) with:
   ```python
   def run_job(ctx: Context, job: str, *, tags: tuple[str, ...] = (),
               lock_timeout: float = CLI_WAIT) -> JobResult:
       """Run one job under the ops lock, record it, alert, and for a backup ping the dead-man's
       switch: /start first, then the URL itself or /fail. The CLI waits for the lock (the default);
       the loop passes 0. A lock still held means another run is busy: BUSY. A restic exit 11 (the
       repository is locked, as while the NAS's retention task runs) is busy too: LOCKED, which
       starts with BUSY. Neither is recorded or alerted, and neither sends /fail (a backup has
       sent /start before an exit 11, and its dead-man's switch decides)."""
       with ExitStack() as stack:
           try:
               stack.enter_context(Locks(ctx.state.locks_dir, timeout=lock_timeout).hold(OPS_LOCK))
           except LockTimeout:
               log.info("%s: %s", job, BUSY)
               return JobResult(job, False, BUSY)
           except FAILURES as exc:  # the lock file can't be opened: a failure, said as any is
               log.debug("%s failed", job, exc_info=True)
               return _conclude(ctx, _alert_config(ctx), job, ctx.clock(), False, failure_detail(exc))
           return _run_held(ctx, job, tags)


   def _trim_runs(ctx: Context) -> None:
       """Once a day: drop runs older than KEEP_RUNS, but never a job's newest run or its newest good
       one, so Status never reads "never succeeded" after a long failing streak. A failure here is
       only logged."""
       now = ctx.clock()
       try:
           last = ctx.state.meta("ops_runs_trimmed")
           if last and timedelta(0) <= now - datetime.fromisoformat(last) < PRUNE_RUNS_EVERY:
               return
           gone = ctx.state.prune_runs(now - KEEP_RUNS)
           ctx.state.set_meta("ops_runs_trimmed", now.isoformat())
       except (*FAILURES, ValueError):
           log.warning("could not trim the old runs")
           return
       if gone:
           log.info("trimmed %d old runs", gone)


   def run_due(ctx: Context) -> list[JobResult]:
       """One pass of the loop: each job that is due, in ORDER, never waiting for the ops lock. A
       busy job is BUSY, and the next pass tries it again."""
       try:
           ctx.state.set_meta("ops_heartbeat", ctx.clock().isoformat())
       except FAILURES:  # a broken state disk must not stop the pass: the jobs still run
           log.warning("could not write the heartbeat")
       _trim_runs(ctx)
       now = ctx.clock()
       return [run_job(ctx, job, lock_timeout=0)
               for job in due(ctx.state, now, enabled_jobs(ctx.cfg), ctx.attempts)
               if not (job in ctx.locked and timedelta(0) <= now - ctx.locked[job] < RETRY_AFTER)]


   def loop(ctx: Context, *, tick: float = 60.0, sleep=time.sleep, stop=lambda: False) -> None:
       """The backup service's main loop: what is due, then a minute's sleep, forever.
       `recordings ops --loop` runs it inside sigterm_forwarded: `docker stop` passes SIGTERM on to a
       running restic or rsync, and once that has stopped, the loop stops too."""
       while not stop():
           try:
               for result in run_due(ctx):
                   log.info("%s: %s (%s)", result.job, "ok" if result.ok else "not ok", result.detail)
           except Exception as exc:  # due() reading a broken state.db, or a bug: wait a tick, retry
               log.warning("a pass of the loop failed (%s)", failure_detail(exc))
               log.debug("a pass of the loop failed", exc_info=True)  # the traceback, for --debug only
           sleep(tick)
   ```

6. **Change `run_child`** (Task 11's) so that Ctrl-C stops the child and waits within the caller's
   timeout. restic handles INT then TERM cleanly (exit 130, no lock left).
   - **Add** before `def run_child(`:
     ```python
     INTERRUPT_GRACE = 120.0  # seconds a child gets to clean up after Ctrl-C when the caller set no timeout


     def _stop_child(proc: subprocess.Popen, deadline: float | None) -> None:
         """After Ctrl-C: SIGTERM the child (restic and rsync stop cleanly on it, whatever signal the
         terminal sent them), then wait for it within what is left of the caller's timeout, or
         INTERRUPT_GRACE with none, and kill it when that runs out. A further Ctrl-C while it cleans up
         is ignored: abandoning it there is what leaves restic's repository lock behind."""
         proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
         wait = INTERRUPT_GRACE if deadline is None else max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)
         end = time.monotonic() + wait
         while True:
             try:
                 proc.communicate(timeout=max(end - time.monotonic(), 0.0))
                 return
             except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                 proc.kill()
                 proc.communicate()
                 return
             except KeyboardInterrupt:
                 continue  # the child is already stopping: let it finish
     ```

In `packages/core/tests/test_backup.py`, **replace** Task 11's
`test_ctrl_c_waits_for_the_child_to_finish_its_cleanup_before_it_propagates` (its child has no
SIGTERM handler, so it now dies before it can clean up) with these three, which come after
`sigterm_when_ready` and `CLEANS_UP`:
```python
def test_ctrl_c_stops_the_child_with_sigterm_and_waits_for_its_cleanup(tmp_path):
    # why: at a terminal, Ctrl-C reaches restic as well. KeyboardInterrupt inside communicate()
    # closed the pipes before waiting, so restic could die of SIGPIPE in the middle of its
    # cleanup and leave its repository lock behind. Now the child is sent SIGTERM (restic handles
    # INT then TERM cleanly, exiting 130) and run_child waits for it before Ctrl-C goes on.
    ready, cleaned = tmp_path / "ready", tmp_path / "cleaned"
    sigterm_when_ready(ready, signal.SIGINT)
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        ops.run_child([sys.executable, "-c", CLEANS_UP % {"ready": str(ready), "cleaned": str(cleaned)}],
                      capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    assert cleaned.exists()  # run_child told it to stop, waited, and only then let Ctrl-C through


def test_a_second_ctrl_c_does_not_abandon_a_child_that_is_cleaning_up(tmp_path):
    # why: a second Ctrl-C used to leave the block, close the pipes and abandon restic mid-cleanup.
    # The child's TERM handler touches `stopping` first, so the second Ctrl-C always lands while
    # _stop_child waits (Popen.communicate has its own 0.25 s wait after the first one).
    ready, cleaned = tmp_path / "ready", tmp_path / "cleaned"
    stopping = tmp_path / "stopping"
    announced = CLEANS_UP.replace("def stop(*_):\n",
                                  "def stop(*_):\n    pathlib.Path(%(stopping)r).touch()\n")
    child = announced % {"ready": str(ready), "cleaned": str(cleaned), "stopping": str(stopping)}
    sigterm_when_ready(ready, signal.SIGINT)  # the first, as soon as the child is up
    main_thread = threading.main_thread().ident

    def second():
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
        while not stopping.exists() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.01)
        time.sleep(0.1)  # the child's 0.5 s cleanup has begun
        signal.pthread_kill(main_thread, signal.SIGINT)

    threading.Thread(target=second, daemon=True).start()
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        ops.run_child([sys.executable, "-c", child], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    assert cleaned.exists()


def test_ctrl_c_keeps_the_callers_timeout_and_kills_a_child_that_ignores_sigterm(tmp_path):
    # why: the wait after Ctrl-C was unbounded and dropped the caller's timeout, so a hung child
    # held the CLI for ever.
    ready = tmp_path / "ready"
    child = ("import pathlib, signal, time\n"
             "signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)\n"
             f"pathlib.Path({str(ready)!r}).touch()\n"
             "time.sleep(60)\n")
    sigterm_when_ready(ready, signal.SIGINT)
    began = time.monotonic()
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        ops.run_child([sys.executable, "-c", child], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=2)
    assert time.monotonic() - began < 8  # about the 2 s timeout, not the child's 60


def test_ctrl_c_with_no_timeout_waits_only_interrupt_grace_for_a_child_that_ignores_sigterm(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(ops, "INTERRUPT_GRACE", 1.0)
    ready = tmp_path / "ready"
    child = ("import pathlib, signal, time\n"
             "signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)\n"
             f"pathlib.Path({str(ready)!r}).touch()\n"
             "time.sleep(60)\n")
    sigterm_when_ready(ready, signal.SIGINT)
    began = time.monotonic()
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        ops.run_child([sys.executable, "-c", child], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert time.monotonic() - began < 8  # about the 1 s grace, not the child's 60
```
(The first two use Task 11's `CLEANS_UP` and `sigterm_when_ready`.)

```python
def cmd_ops(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    ctx = _ops_context(args.json)
    if isinstance(ctx, int):
        return ctx
    if args.loop:
        ctx.retry_lock = None  # §15.1: the loop never waits for restic's lock; the CLI does
        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
        # docker stop: SIGTERM goes on to a running restic or rsync, which stops cleanly and
        # drops its lock; then this process stops. The job it was in is neither recorded nor
        # alerted, and the next start runs it again.
        with ops.sigterm_forwarded():
            ops.loop(ctx)
        return 0
    with ops.sigterm_forwarded():
        results = ops.run_due(ctx)
    _emit({"ran": [{"job": r.job, "ok": r.ok, "detail": r.detail} for r in results]}, args.json)
    failed = [r for r in results if not r.ok]
    if failed and all(r.detail.startswith(ops.BUSY) for r in failed):
        return 75  # EX_TEMPFAIL, as _job_result: every turn was busy (the ops lock, or restic's)
    return 1 if failed else 0


def cmd_alert_test(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    cfg = _config(args.json)
    if isinstance(cfg, int):
        return cfg
    try:
        ac = alerts.from_config(cfg, os.environ)
    except config.ConfigError as exc:
        return _fail(str(exc), args.json, 78)
    if ac.topic and not ac.ntfy_server:
        return _fail("RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC is set but [alerts] ntfy_server is not", args.json, 78)
    if not ac.enabled and not ac.deadman_url:
        return _fail("set [alerts] ntfy_server and RECORDINGS_NTFY_TOPIC_FILE, or "
                     "RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL_FILE, first", args.json, 78)
    # Each part is tested when it is set up: null is "not configured", false is "failed".
    sent = alerts.send(ac, title="recordings: test alert", message="If you see this, alerts work.",
                       priority=3, tags=("white_check_mark",)) if ac.enabled else None
    # /log records the test without changing the check's state, so it can never hide an outage.
    logged = (alerts.ping_deadman(ac, "log", message="recordings alert-test")
              if ac.deadman_url else None)
    _emit({"ntfy": sent, "deadman": logged}, args.json)
    return 0 if sent is not False and logged is not False else 1
```
with `"ops": cmd_ops, "alert-test": cmd_alert_test,` in `commands`.

```toml
# RECORDINGS_DEADMAN_URL(_FILE), below. The topic is 20 to 64 random letters, digits, - or _: with
```
